newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Australia's two international airlines, Qantas Airways and Ansett International, are having trouble coping with the sharp increase in their frequent flyer liabilities, as membership of their loyalty schemes spirals towards the two million mark. Strong commercial networking by both airlines has seen up to 30,000 new members signing up each month. Page 1.

Standards Australia, the national standards body, is behind the push by Government bodies and industry to introduce a scheme of secure identification for electronic commerce on the Internet. The plan will be released tomorrow and will put the Federal Govrnment under pressure to create legislation that will permit the new system to replace signatures. Page 3.

A move by Queensland Independent MP Liz Cunningham to stifle key elements of a legislative package aimed at restructuring Queensland's workers' compensation system has been criticised by employer groups. Queensland Chamber of Commerce and Industry
head Cive Bubb says business confidence would be damaged and jobs may be lost if the proposal does not go through. Page 5.

After narrowly surviving a no-confidence motion brought against it after allegations of corruption, the Queensland Government is again under fire, with the State's Criminal Justice Commission investigating Queensland Police Minister Russell Cooper's alleged involement in a deal with Queensland prison officers before the Coalition gained power earlier in the year. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following a major tax crackdown on individuals and after the cash economy fell A$660 million, or 82.5 per cent short of target, the Australian Taxation Office has conceded it may have gone too far in taking some pressure off big business in the early 1990, and will now step up its attacks on Australia's top companies. Page 1.

Queensland's Criminal Justice Commission has launched an inquiry into allegations that Police and Corrective Services Minister Russell Cooper and Matthew Heery, a National Party worker who figured prominently in the Carruthers inquiry into possible electoal bribery, encouraged prison officers to prolong a State-wide jail strike in the lead-up to the Mundingburra by-election. Page 1.

In the midst of the debate over race and immigration triggered by comments from controversial Federal Independent MP Pauline Hanson, the Housing Industry Association has announced it will start a campaign to convince the Howard Government and the Australin public of the need for a higher immigration intake. Page 1.
New South Wales Roads Minister Michael Knight announced a A$520 million upgrade for Sydney's M5 motorway yesterday, in a
plan which will see the new M5 East in Sydney's south built
without a toll and which will mean drivers will face only two
sets of trafic lights between the Harbour Bridge and Albury on the Victorian border. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following a warning from the Australian Tourism Commission that the country's A$14 billion tourism industry was at risk unless the perception of racial disharmony could be dispelled, the Tourism Task Force, which represents executives from 100 tourism andtransport companies, has called on Prime Minister John Howard to fund a A$25 million marketing "rescue package" to combat the growing Asian backlash over the race row. Page 1.

Under a proposal sure to spark vigorous public debate, the Sydney City Council has received a development application requesting that the Sydney Tower, the tallest landmark in the city's high-rise horizon, feature a giant four-storey, coloured neon sign wth the official Olympic boomerang athlete logo on one side and AMP on the other. Page 1.

As American research indicates children are nearly three times more likely to suffer attention deficit hyperactivity disorder if their mothers smoked during pregnancy, new Australian research, conducted in the Hunter region, has highlighted major flaws inthe diagnosis and management of the disease, suggesting many children are not getting the best care. Page 1.

The New South Wales regulation review committee, which oversees the legality of legislation and Government legislation, has opposed the views of New South Wales Police Minister Paul Whelan by claiming the State's gun control strategy in the six months sine the Port Arthur massacre may have been based on a flawed law, which would then class it as invalid. Page 3.
THE AGE

A comprehensive examination of Victoria's schooling system by the Age has found that the State's primary and secondary schools are struggling to cope with sweeping changes, with teachers reporting high levels of stress and educationalists warning the divie between State and private schools is widening. Page A1.

Australia's former leading horse trainer Colin Hayes has warned horses' performance would improve dramatically and possibly hide other stimulants when their bicarbonate levels are over 35.0, which is two points below what is now legal in
Victoria. Hayes questions any opposition to the lowering of the legal levels from 37.0 to 35.0. Page A1.

Kevin Prendergast, the trainer of this year's Melbourne Cup favourite Oscar Schindler, believes everything is falling into place for his horse, as rain in Melbourne softened the track. Prendergast had threatened to scratch the Irish contender from the rae if the track remained hard - the track's softening has now increased the chances of the horse becoming only the second northern-hemisphere-trained winner of tomorrow's race. Page A1.

Tourism Taskforce chairman John Brown has, on behalf of the tourism industry, called for a A$25 million marketing campaign to promote Australia in Asia and dispel fears Asians may have about visiting Australia in the wake of the race debate sparked by outpoken Independent MP Pauline Hanson. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
